_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS ROUND 1081's REPAIRS ARE NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
The gate in this crate proves ITSELF with `tests/gate.rs`, which puts each
shape into a throwaway workspace and reads the verdict. This file proves the
other half: that the four waits it made this repository delete were load-
bearing, and that what replaced them still fails when the thing it waits for
does not happen. A repair that removes a sleep and leaves a test green for a
NEW wrong reason is the failure mode here, and `zero_rate_sampling_drops_
all_spans` is where it would live — an assertion of ABSENCE passes when the
path it forbids was never exercised.
The test command is scoped to the targets the repairs touch, and it carries
four of these five targets compile to nothing: R1081 measured six of this
crate's integration test targets running `0 tests` under the workspace suite
CI has been running, which is how a 50ms `sleep` called a 'tiny grace' lived
in `grpc_mtls_smoke.rs` without anything ever executing it.

injections.name: the-zero-rate-test-is-shown-what-it-forbids
injections.why: an absence proves nothing about a path that was never exercised; with the sampler at 1.0 the SAME quiesce chain must carry spans all the way to the collector, so a red here is what says the zero-rate green was a measurement rather than a silence

injections.name: the-rotation-retry-is-given-nothing-to-succeed-at
injections.why: the sleep this replaced made the test's green a claim that the acceptor published within 50ms; the retry must instead be unable to pass at all when the rotation never happens, and it must say so by exhausting the named budget rather than by hanging

injections.name: the-audit-append-stops-publishing-to-subscribers
injections.why: R1081 replaced a 200ms timed `recv` with a wait-free `try_recv`, which asserts the STRONGER property that the record is already in the subscriber's buffer when the append returns; removing the publish must make that fail at once, and the live-tail target going red with it is the same claim seen from the gRPC side. THE NAMES ARE MODULE-QUALIFIED because that is how the harness reads a unit test out of libtest's output — the first run of this file aimed at the bare name, was told `did not reach it`, and the answer was to correct the address rather than to relax the expectation
